k4-session-start.title: C4: decide_session_start's argument tested, not read
k4-session-start.imperative: Determine by test whether a per-agent key from a DIFFERENT agent can reach the merged session_view at SessionStart. #419 read-through is the claimed mechanism; establish whether it is true or merely plausible.
k4-session-start.finding: FAIL (B2). The argument is FALSE in the sense that matters, and I measured it rather than read it (/tmp/g3rev/c4_session_start.py, OLD 999b7663 vs NEW, six constructed cases). The claim is 'every entry in the merged view was claimed by THIS session, under its bare key or under a per-agent key of its own'. session_view merges the bare sid PLUS every sid#<agent_id> key (_session_keys, spine_rail.py:515), and Agent-tool subagents SHARE the parent's session_id -- that sharing is the entire premise of #419 and of the per-agent key. So a DIFFERENT agent's per-agent key is in the merged view by construction. 'A per-agent key of its own' conflates 'of this harness session' with 'of this agent'; the handoff named exactly this and the answer is: yes, it can reach the view, and the site now resumes from an entry the acting agent does not own. MEASURED. Case 2 -- crew claimed a spine in ANOTHER worktree and its key leads; the PARENT's session starts: OLD resumed the parent from its OWN gate (PARENT-MARKER), NEW resumes it from the CREW's gate (CREW-MARKER). That is a REGRESSION introduced by this gate, and it is the #549/#419 bug class itself -- an agent handed another agent's gate with 'Pick the run back up at this gate and drive it through the engine'. Case 3 -- only a crew's per-agent key exists and the parent never claimed anything: OLD injected no context, NEW injects the CREW's gate. Case 1 -- in-tree crew: OLD and NEW both wrongly give the crew's gate, so the defect class pre-exists for in-tree crews; this change WIDENS it to out-of-tree crews. Case 6 -- identical binding with the parent's key written FIRST: both give PARENT-MARKER. So selection here is purely dict/claim order with NO ownership preference. That is precisely the hazard the implementer itself wrote into decide_stop's own comment -- 'Order alone would hand a Commander whichever entry happened to be claimed first -- routinely its in-tree crew's' -- and it was fixed at that site and not at this one. Case 5 -- even when the payload carries an agent_id, this site ignores it. THE FIX IS THE ONE ALREADY WRITTEN AT THE OTHER SITE: prefer the entry whose session_view_provenance key equals binding_key(payload), falling back only when the session owns none. With no agent_id in the payload binding_key is the bare sid, which selects the session's own entry and repairs cases 1, 2 and 3.

r6-fowler.finding: Pass run over 999b7663..e3e50a69 plus the evidence harness. All 12 baseline smells given a verdict; verifier exits 0 (smells=12, flagged=[long-method, duplicated-code, comments-as-deodorant], overridden=[primitive-obsession]). Three flagged, and each ties to a finding rather than being decoration: long-method -- decide_stop's new SELECTION step is an inline comprehension inside an already-long function, and extracting it as _select_entry_for(mid_flight, owners, own_key) is literally the same edit as the B2 fix, because that is the rule decide_session_start is missing; duplicated-code -- m4_differential.py re-implements the test file's fixtures and re-derives its own base, which is how its BEFORE arm drifted into self-comparison (B1), and it stands in pointed contrast to tests/test_worktree_derivation.py in this same lane, which was deliberately built so a missing copy fails collection; comments-as-deodorant -- the section header asserts binding-key provenance decides ownership at both sites while one site does no comparison at all (B3). One override, primitive-obsession, logged with the standard (stdlib-only hook plus the documented single-composer discipline for binding_key and _AGENT_ID_ALLOWED) and the reason (the one-place property a key type would buy is already bought, and a class in a hook whose failure deadlocks every turn costs more than the untyped string).

findings: k3-differential: FAIL (B1). The shipped differential is self-comparing as committed. crew-handoffs/g3-implement/m4_differential.py:23 sets BASE_REV = git rev-parse HEAD, so its BEFORE arm loads the hook at whatever HEAD is when it runs -- not the pinned pre-change base its own docstring names ('BEFORE the change (git HEAD 999b7663)'). It was honest only at authoring time, when HEAD happened to be 999b7663. The change is now committed, so re-running it today loads ca577709's hook as BEFORE, i.e. the post-change hook on both arms. I ran it as the handoff instructs: header prints 'BEFORE (ca577709)' and EVERY row comes back identical, including all three newly-blocking rows the criterion asks me to spot-check. S3/S4/S8 read 'BEFORE BLOCK / AFTER BLOCK' -- the exact opposite of the truth, and it reads as confirmation. This is CREW_CONTEXT 'a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed' and global-everyone 'pin a claim to the revision you read it at'. FIX: one line, BASE_REV = '999b7663' (or derive the parent of the commit that last touched the hook). THE UNDERLYING CLAIMS ARE TRUE. I pinned a copy to 999b7663 and re-ran the implementer's own harness: S1 foreign-owner/NOTHING -> own-gate/PARENT-MARKER; S2 foreign-owner/NOTHING -> own-gate/CREW-MARKER; S3 ALLOWED -> BLOCK own-gate/OWN-MARKER; S4 ALLOWED -> BLOCK foreign-owner/NOTHING; S5 no-context -> INJECT RESUME-MARKER; S6 six garbage rows BLOCK/BLOCK; S7 own-gate/FAILSAFE -> foreign-owner/NOTHING; S8 ALLOWED -> BLOCK own-gate/PLATFORM-MARKER. My independent differential agrees on every one. HAND SPOT-CHECK of the three newly-blocking rows against the code, per the criterion: S3 -- old _entry_mid_flight_view called _foreign_worktree(data, entry), cwd and worktree both truthy and _same_path False, returned True, entry skipped, mid_flight empty, return {} = allow; new signature takes no payload so there is no skip, entry is mid-flight, owners.get(path) is the bare 's1' and binding_key({'session_id':'s1',...}) is 's1', _is_own_entry True, own-gate rendering. S4 -- crew's entry is filed under CREW_KEY with the crew's own tree; old _foreign_worktree True, skipped, allow; new blocks, owners.get is CREW_KEY vs own_key SID, _is_own_entry False, the 'own' list is empty so it falls back to mid_flight[0] and takes the foreign-owner branch, imperative withheld from both reason and additionalContext. S8 -- old _same_path folds through normcase, identity on POSIX, so 'C:\\Foo\\wt' vs 'c:/foo/wt' differ here and match on Windows: platform-dependent allow/block; new never reads worktree, blocks on both. All three verified by reading, not only by running.

k4-session-start: FAIL (B2). The argument is FALSE in the sense that matters, and I measured it rather than read it (/tmp/g3rev/c4_session_start.py, OLD 999b7663 vs NEW, six constructed cases). The claim is 'every entry in the merged view was claimed by THIS session, under its bare key or under a per-agent key of its own'. session_view merges the bare sid PLUS every sid#<agent_id> key (_session_keys, spine_rail.py:515), and Agent-tool subagents SHARE the parent's session_id -- that sharing is the entire premise of #419 and of the per-agent key. So a DIFFERENT agent's per-agent key is in the merged view by construction. 'A per-agent key of its own' conflates 'of this harness session' with 'of this agent'; the handoff named exactly this and the answer is: yes, it can reach the view, and the site now resumes from an entry the acting agent does not own. MEASURED. Case 2 -- crew claimed a spine in ANOTHER worktree and its key leads; the PARENT's session starts: OLD resumed the parent from its OWN gate (PARENT-MARKER), NEW resumes it from the CREW's gate (CREW-MARKER). That is a REGRESSION introduced by this gate, and it is the #549/#419 bug class itself -- an agent handed another agent's gate with 'Pick the run back up at this gate and drive it through the engine'. Case 3 -- only a crew's per-agent key exists and the parent never claimed anything: OLD injected no context, NEW injects the CREW's gate. Case 1 -- in-tree crew: OLD and NEW both wrongly give the crew's gate, so the defect class pre-exists for in-tree crews; this change WIDENS it to out-of-tree crews. Case 6 -- identical binding with the parent's key written FIRST: both give PARENT-MARKER. So selection here is purely dict/claim order with NO ownership preference. That is precisely the hazard the implementer itself wrote into decide_stop's own comment -- 'Order alone would hand a Commander whichever entry happened to be claimed first -- routinely its in-tree crew's' -- and it was fixed at that site and not at this one. Case 5 -- even when the payload carries an agent_id, this site ignores it. THE FIX IS THE ONE ALREADY WRITTEN AT THE OTHER SITE: prefer the entry whose session_view_provenance key equals binding_key(payload), falling back only when the session owns none. With no agent_id in the payload binding_key is the bare sid, which selects the session's own entry and repairs cases 1, 2 and 3.

k10-claim-not-symbol: FAIL (B3), and it is a claim, not a symbol -- the symbol side is clean. worktree_from_spine_path appears 0 times in scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py and tests/test_spine_rail.py. Repo-wide two remain, both outside allowed scope and both TRUE prose recording the deletion (tests/test_worktree_derivation.py:14, tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py:451). I then read each replacement passage WHOLE and tested each sentence against the tree. _worktree_from_spine's new docstring: 'This is the ONE implementation of the rule in the repo' -- TRUE, verified, IMPLEMENTATIONS in tests/test_worktree_derivation.py has the single entry 'hook', checklist_engine.py's two remaining mentions are prose pointers and line 3507 says outright the engine holds no copy, and spine_lifecycle.py:96 likewise. 'Its specification is the shared case table ... which drives this function directly' -- TRUE, _require(_HOOK, '_worktree_from_spine') raises at collection if the symbol goes. 'deleted in #609 g2 under ADMIRAL_RULING-2 N2' -- corroborated. 'It will re-land as a COPY, not an import' -- consistent with the stdlib-only constraint. tests/test_spine_rail.py:832-839's replacement passage -- TRUE, and its _same_path caller claim checks out. THE UNTRUE SENTENCE is in the new section header, scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py:685-687: 'Ownership is decided by binding-key provenance at both former call sites -- see decide_stop and decide_session_start.' It is not. At decide_session_start nothing compares a provenance key to anything; the site takes the first entry in dict order (spine_rail.py:1685-1689) and my k4 measurement shows it selecting entries the acting agent does not own. The site's own inline comment is more careful ('Membership in the view IS the binding-key answer at this site'), but the section header states the stronger claim and a reader arriving at this module reads the header first. This is exactly the defect class the handoff warned about: the symbol is gone and the false claim survived in the replacement prose. Related and softer: OwnershipIsBindingKeyNotWorktree's docstring says giving parent and crew different trees 'proves nothing about this change'; for the SessionStart site that is wrong -- the differing-tree case is precisely where the deleted test was doing real work and where the new code regresses (k4 case 2).

r1-handoff: Mostly yes, with two substantive gaps. The gate's stated task -- delete _foreign_worktree with both call sites and decide ownership by binding-key provenance -- is done, and done well at decide_stop: the #549 shape is genuinely exercised on a shared tree, the red reproduces against 999b7663, the fail-safe direction survives every garbage input I could construct, and the rendering distinction is now sharper than before. The handoff required each site's before/after stated separately and what newly blocks enumerated; both were delivered and both reproduce. FAILS ON TWO of the handoff's own close criteria. (1) Criterion 4: decide_session_start's replacement is not sound. 'Membership in the merged view IS the binding-key answer' is false -- session_view merges every sid#<agent_id> key and subagents share the parent's session_id, so another agent's entry is in the view by construction, and the site selects by dict order with no ownership test at all. Measured regression: a crew that claimed in another worktree now displaces the parent's own binding at SessionStart, where the deleted tree test was getting it right. (2) Criterion 3: the shipped differential pins its BEFORE arm to 'git rev-parse HEAD', so now that the change is committed it compares the change against itself and every row reads identical. The handoff asked the reviewer to run it; running it as shipped tells you nothing.

r3-evidence: Evidence is largely strong and reproduces, with one broken artifact. REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY: the targeted red (8 failed / 3 passed against a scratch checkout of 999b7663's hook), the full suite (3177/5/0, cache cleared, env scrubbed), tests/test_worktree_derivation.py green and unedited, the import block identical, the +7 arithmetic reconciled against the diff, and every before/after row once the differential's base is pinned correctly. I ALSO READ ALL EIGHT REWORKED TESTS as the handoff demanded, looking for a weakened assertion, and found none -- the three flips all STRENGTHEN (out == {} becomes block plus a marker assertion; test_binding_worktree_comes_from_resolved_spine_in_real_linked_worktree now additionally asserts the owner key is named and the child's imperative is withheld from BOTH rendered fields), and the device swaps replace a foreign worktree with a genuinely unreadable target, which is honest. The repaired test (test_session_start_unreadable_skip_bound_reinject_fallback_reinject) is markedly better than what it replaced: real nested bind() shape, the readable leg placed outside the scan's reach, an explicit _scan_active_spine == [] guard, and a marker assertion, so only the binding can explain the result. Two bookkeeping notes: the result says three tests had used a foreign worktree as a device and I count four (test_session_start_bind_on_resume_still_writes_under_the_bare_key is the fourth); and the 'null worktree' row of test_garbage_location_data_never_relaxes_the_rail does not write a null worktree because bind() substitutes str(project_dir) for None. FAIL is carried by the differential: crew-handoffs/g3-implement/m4_differential.py:23 takes its BEFORE arm from git rev-parse HEAD rather than the pinned base, so as committed it is a check that cannot fail. See k3.

r4-quality: Per constraint. (a) Fail-safe not fail-open: PASS -- 0 regressions across 26 constructed rows, _is_own_entry survives an exploding __eq__ and returns False, which withholds rather than relaxes. (b) Nudge / 3-strike hatch keyed by sid alone: PASS -- single aggregated nudges[sid] record, asserted with two mid-flight entries present. (c) stdlib only in spine_rail.py: PASS -- 11 imports, byte-identical. (d) #549's two-way rendering survives: PASS, and is sharper. (e) tests/test_worktree_derivation.py unedited: PASS. FAIL is on the repo's own documented standards rather than on the handoff's five constraints. CREW_CONTEXT 'Verification Discipline' -- 'a check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed' -- is violated by the committed differential (k3). CREW_CONTEXT 'Assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it' has its mirror image here: the new section-header comment at spine_rail.py:685-687 asserts ownership is decided by binding-key provenance at BOTH call sites, and the code at one of them does not do that (k10). global-everyone 'Pin a claim to the revision you read it at' is violated by the same rev-parse HEAD (k3). Code quality otherwise is high: _is_own_entry is a small named predicate with its two asymmetric missing-key readings documented and justified, the deletion is pinned by a test so a re-landing is deliberate, and the signature narrowing of _entry_mid_flight_view honestly expresses that the site no longer reads the payload.
consolidation.summary: BLOCK on three findings, one of them substantive. The gate's core change is correct and well evidenced at decide_stop: _foreign_worktree is genuinely deleted with both call sites, the #549 shape is exercised on a real shared tree with the parent carrying no agent_id and the crew carrying one, the claimed red reproduces independently against 999b7663 (8 failed / 3 passed), the fail-safe posture survives every garbage input I could construct (0 regressions across 26 rows, _is_own_entry never raises even on an exploding __eq__), the nudge hatch stays keyed by sid alone, the import block is byte-identical, _same_path keeps real callers, tests/test_worktree_derivation.py is unedited and green, and the suite is 3177/5/0 with the +7 arithmetic reconciled against the diff. B2 (blocking): decide_session_start's replacement is unsound. The claim that membership in the merged view IS the binding-key answer is false -- session_view merges every sid#<agent_id> key and subagents share the parent's session_id -- and the site selects purely by claim order with no ownership test. Measured: a crew that claimed in another worktree now displaces the parent's own binding at SessionStart, which the deleted worktree test was getting right; and a session with no binding of its own now resumes from a crew's spine. That is the #549/#419 bug class reappearing at the other call site, in a gate whose whole purpose is to end it. B1: the shipped differential takes its BEFORE arm from git rev-parse HEAD, so now that the change is committed it compares the change against itself and every row -- including all three the criterion asks a reviewer to spot-check -- reads identical. B3: the new section header asserts binding-key provenance decides ownership at both call sites; at one of them nothing is compared. All three fixes are small and known. On the open decision the gate hands back, I do not agree the sites are asymmetric: they are asymmetric about BLOCKING and identical about SELECTION.

triage_candidates.statement: SessionStart scan-bind binds a session to a spine it never claimed. When a session has no binding, decide_session_start falls through to _scan_active_spine and, on exactly one active-leased spine, WRITES a binding for that session and injects 'drive this gate'. A run_crew.py-launched crew has its own session_id and no binding, so the single active spine it finds is its parent Commander's, under the parent's live lease. Binding-key provenance cannot fix it because there is no binding key yet at scan time; the discriminator would have to be the engine lease's owner. Independently confirmed: my own SessionStart context told me to reload the commander skill and drive the parent's execute.json. Reported by the g3 implementer as its observation 1; I reproduce the diagnosis and second it. Needs an authority decision and touches the scan-bind path, not this gate's two call sites.

A Stop payload carrying agent_id: null would now be told its own gate is foreign. binding_key reads a present-but-null agent_id as UNUSABLE rather than absent, so _is_own_entry matches nothing and the agent gets #549's foreign-owner wording with its own imperative withheld -- where the pre-change hook rendered the imperative. Measured (rows A1-A4 of my differential). It never relaxes the rail, so it is not a constraint violation, and the pinned probe capture shows the harness OMITS the key entirely for a top-level agent, so the shape is hypothetical today. Worth recording because if a harness version ever starts sending an explicit null, every top-level agent is permanently told 'not your gate to drive' until the 3-strike hatch opens.

tests/test_spine_rail.py's bind() helper silently substitutes str(project_dir) when worktree=None, so the 'null worktree' row of test_garbage_location_data_never_relaxes_the_rail does not exercise a null worktree -- it degenerates into the trivial same-tree case. The behaviour is safe (verified separately: a genuine null worktree blocks before and after), but the row proves something other than its label, inside a loop whose count assertion reads as though six distinct shapes were covered.
